question.problem:
Find the median of the random variable $X$ if the probability density function of $X$ is given by

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{98}{{x}^{3}},\, & x\ge 7, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The median of a random variable $X$ is the number $m$ such that

$$
P(X\le m)=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le m) & ={\int }_{7}^{m}\frac{98}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{49}{{x}^{2}}|}_{7}^{m} \\  & =1-\frac{49}{{m}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the median is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{49}{{m}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{49}{{m}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{2} \\ m & =7\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we took the positive root because $m>7.$
